messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a weird perf regression in the nightly replay runs after we switched the CUDA base image for the GPU smoke pool. Throughput dropped ~18% on the 1k token scenario. Anyone else seeing this?

aj: saw the alert. which image/tag? :eyes:

maria: docker.redwood/gpu-infer:cuda12-optimized-2026-03. Regression only showed up when we used the new image + kernel flags we flipped yesterday.

leo: interesting. on which GPU? A100 or A10G?

maria: A100 for the smoke runs. reproduced on a bare-metal node and in k8s.

sara: can you share the perf profile? I can look at kernels.

maria: pasted the short trace from perf-tooling (trimmed):

```
2026-03-12 03:12:02 profile start
matmul_opt_kernel (fast)  -> 12%
matmul_generic (fallback) -> 47%  <-- large jump
kv_cache_lookup          -> 18%
attention_fused          -> 9%
other                  -> 14%
profile end
```

maria: older image (cuda11-based) had matmul_opt_kernel ~55% and generic <5%.

aj: that suggests kernel selector is picking fallback kernels on cuda12 image. Could be different cuBLAS or libcudnn version or missing nvml flags.

leo: also check glibc and linker paths — sometimes a different symbol results in our custom kernel loader failing and falling back. We had a tiny loader msg earlier but log level was info only.

maria: here's the debug line I found in runtime stdout: `KernelSelector WARNING: failed to load cuBLAS-compat plugin, falling back to generic matmul`

infra-bot: docker image scanned: docker.redwood/gpu-infer:cuda12-optimized-2026-03 -> cuBLAS 12.1.0 detected, libcudnn 9.0.0, kernel-rt flags: rmm-locking=on

leo: can you try pinning the cuBLAS plugin path explicitly? Also check that LD_LIBRARY_PATH has /usr/local/cuda/lib64 before system libs.

maria: I ran a quick AB between images with replay harness (same trace):
- cuda11-image: 1k tokens @ 1300 qps sustained
- cuda12-image: 1k tokens @ 1050 qps sustained

sara: KV cache % looks higher in the trace — is eviction rate up? If KV lookups are slower, it pushes more work into matmul fallback.

maria: eviction rate was same, but cache hit latency doubled. sample log: `kv_cache lookup latency=0.9ms -> 2.1ms`

aj: could be NUMA binding or a different kernel param in the image (I remember we toggled `vm.swappiness` in the new image).

leo: what about thread-affinity / OMP_NUM_THREADS? New image may set defaults via /etc/profile.d.

maria: checked — OMP_NUM_THREADS not set. but /proc/sys/kernel/threads-max is the same.

sara: suggested repro steps: 1) run replay harness with --trace-id <id> on cuda11-image and cuda12-image; 2) enable KERNEL_SEL_DEBUG=1 env; 3) capture nvprof/cupti summary; 4) check ldconfig -p for cublas path.

maria: doing that now, will upload artifacts. Also temporary mitigation: pin runtime config to `kernel_selector: prefer_opt=false` to avoid triggering the broken path until we root-cause. That recovers throughput to ~1260 qps.

aj: +1 for the temporary knob. We should also add an automated test in the replay harness: run a small smoke compare across images whenever we publish a new GPU image.

leo: I'll add a check in the build pipeline to validate our kernel plugin loads (exit non-zero if it can't find plugin). Saves people from subtle fallbacks.

maria: uploaded logs to /shared/replays/1800012345/artifacts.tar.gz — includes nvprof, runtime logs, and container diffs (ldconfig, env, package list).

loadtest-bot: scheduled retest job 1800012400 -> results pending.

sara: postmortem note: when we compare images for env parity, include: cuBLAS/cuDNN exact versions, LD paths, any distro glibc variants, kernel flags, and our runtime kernel plugin compatibility check. That should be an apples-to-apples checklist.

maria: thanks all — will follow up with a short writeup and the quick mitigation change. :thumbsup:

leo: FYI, if anyone wants to reproduce quickly:
```
# repro snippet
docker run --gpus all -e KERNEL_SEL_DEBUG=1 \
  -v /shared/replays:/replays docker.redwood/gpu-infer:cuda12-optimized-2026-03 \
  /opt/runtime/bin/replay --trace /replays/trace-1k.json --stats
```

aj: ping me when artifacts are ready, I can roll the kernel-selector patch. :fire:
